${\eta^{n}}^{n} \stackrel{(\sigma)}{Y}_{n}=\frac{(n+\sigma)!}{2^{2 \sigma} n!\sigma!} i\left(\eta^{\sigma}-\xi^{\sigma}\right)\left[z^{n-\sigma}-\frac{(n-\sigma)(n-\sigma-1)}{4(\sigma+1)} z^{n-\sigma-2} \xi \eta+\right.$ \&c. $]$,
(79)
we find that on performing the differentiations with respect
to $z$, all the terms of the series except the first disappear, and
the factor $(n--\sigma)!$ is introduced.
Continuing the differentiations with respect to $\xi$ and $\eta$ we
get rid also of these variables and introduce the factor $-2 i \sigma!$, so
that the final result is
$$\iint\left(\stackrel{(\sigma)}{Y}_{n}\right)^{2} d s=\frac{8 \pi a^{2}}{2 n+1} \frac{(n+\sigma)!(n-\sigma)!}{2^{2 \sigma} n!n!}$$
(80)
We shall denote the second member of this equation by the
abbreviated symbol $[n, \sigma]$.
This expression is correct for all values of $\sigma$ from 1 to $n$ inclu-
sive, but there is no harmonic in $\sin \sigma \phi$ corresponding to $\sigma=0$.
In the same way we can shew that
$$\iint\left(\stackrel{(\sigma)}{Y}_{n}^{c}\right)^{2} d s=\frac{8 \pi a^{2}}{2 n+1} \frac{(n+\sigma)!(n-\sigma)!}{2^{2 \sigma} n!n!}$$
(81)
for all values of $\sigma$ from 1 to $n$ inclusive.
When $\sigma=0$, the harmonic becomes the zonal harmonic, and
$$\iint\left(\stackrel{(0)}{Y}_{n}^{(0)}\right)^{2} d s=\iint\left(P_{\mathrm{n}}\right)^{2} d s=\frac{4 \pi a^{2}}{2 n+1}$$
(82)
a result which may be obtained directly from equation (50) by
putting $Y_{n}=P_{m}$ and remembering that the value of the zonal
harmonic at its pole is unity.
142 a.] We can now apply the method of Art. 136 to determine
the coefficient of any given tesseral surface harmonic in the
expansion of any arbitrary function of the position of a point on
a sphere. For let $F$ be the arbitrary function, and let $A_{\eta}^{\sigma}$ be the
coefficient of $Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}$ in the expansion of this function in surface
harmonics of the symmetrical system, then
$$\iint F Y_{n}^{(\sigma)} d s=A_{n}^{(\sigma)} \iint\left(Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}\right)^{2} d s=A_{n}^{(\sigma)}[n, \sigma]$$
(83)
where $[n, \sigma]$ is the abbreviation for the value of the surface in-
tegral given in equation (80).
142 b.] Let $\Psi$ be any function which satisfies Laplace's equa-
tion, and which has no singular values within a distance $\alpha$ of a
point $O$, which we may take as the origin of coordinates. It
is always possible to expand such a function in a series of solid
harmonics of positive degree, having their origin at 0 .

Continuing the differentiations with respect to $\xi$ and $\eta$ we

 that the final result is

$$\begin{equation*}
\iint\left(\stackrel{(\sigma)}{Y}_{n}\right)^{2} d s=\frac{8 \pi a^{2}}{2 n+1} \frac{(n+\sigma)!(n-\sigma)!}{2^{2 \sigma} n!n!} \tag{80}
\end{equation*}$$


We shall denote the second member of this equation by the
 abbreviated symbol $[n, \sigma]$.


This expression is correct for all values of $\sigma$ from 1 to $n$ inclu
sive, but there is no harmonic in $\sin \sigma \phi$ corresponding to $\sigma=0$.


In the same way we can shew that

$$\begin{equation*}
\iint\left(\stackrel{(\sigma)}{Y}_{n}^{c}\right)^{2} d s=\frac{8 \pi a^{2}}{2 n+1} \frac{(n+\sigma)!(n-\sigma)!}{2^{2 \sigma} n!n!} \tag{81}
\end{equation*}$$

for all values of $\sigma$ from 1 to $n$ inclusive.

When $\sigma=0$, the harmonic becomes the zonal harmonic, and

$$\begin{equation*}
\iint\left(\stackrel{(0)}{Y}_{n}^{(0)}\right)^{2} d s=\iint\left(P_{\mathrm{n}}\right)^{2} d s=\frac{4 \pi a^{2}}{2 n+1} \tag{82}
\end{equation*}$$

a result which may be obtained directly from equation (50) by
 putting $Y_{n}=P_{m}$ and remembering that the value of the zonal
 harmonic at its pole is unity.


142 a.] We can now apply the method of Art. 136 to determine
 the coefficient of any given tesseral surface harmonic in the
 expansion of any arbitrary function of the position of a point on
 a sphere. For let $F$ be the arbitrary function, and let $A_{\eta}^{\sigma}$ be the
 coefficient of $Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}$ in the expansion of this function in surface
 harmonics of the symmetrical system, then

$$\begin{equation*}
\iint F Y_{n}^{(\sigma)} d s=A_{n}^{(\sigma)} \iint\left(Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}\right)^{2} d s=A_{n}^{(\sigma)}[n, \sigma] \tag{83}
\end{equation*}$$

where $[n, \sigma]$ is the abbreviation for the value of the surface in
tegral given in equation (80).


142 b.] Let $\Psi$ be any function which satisfies Laplace's equa
tion, and which has no singular values within a distance $\alpha$ of a
 point $O$, which we may take as the origin of coordinates. It
 is always possible to expand such a function in a series of solid
 harmonics of positive degree, having their origin at 0 .
